title: Bayesian Wave Function Collapse: Probabilistic Sampling Under Structural Constraints
content: Wave Function Collapse (WFC) generates structurally consistent configurations through sequential assignment and constraint propagation, but its local frequency weights do not generally reproduce a prescribed distribution over feasible configurations. We introduce Bayesian WFC, a probabilistic framework that combines structural priors, hard constraints, and soft preferences within an explicit target distribution. The central insight is that correct collapse probabilities depend on the total probability mass of feasible completions, rather than local pattern frequencies alone. Since exact completion masses are generally intractable, we develop an amortized guide that learns to predict them from exact or importance-weighted Monte Carlo estimates, while sequential importance sampling corrects for bias in the resulting proposals. We establish exact sampling with true completion masses, bound the accumulation of conditional approximation errors, and identify conditions for sound constraint propagation and support preservation. Experiments on enumerated grids demonstrate improved distributional fidelity through learned guidance and importance correction, while larger-grid experiments show improved feasible completion and importance-weight efficiency without exhaustive enumeration. Bayesian WFC thus connects constraint-based generation with principled probabilistic inference, separating structural validity from distributional fidelity, while preserving WFC's sequential construction and constraint propagation mechanisms.
